To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
carcasses of lambs with higher muscularity yield slightly more leg and saddle meat, but this difference is small relative to the greater muscle depth and width of the 'eye' of the hind leg.

lamb carcasses with a superior muscularity index (as defined by the European E class) had a higher yield from boneless leg and saddle cuts and higher muscle to bone in the leg region than carcasses with a lower muscularity index.

the leg and saddle of lambs with superior muscularity yield 4.3 % more meat than those of lambs with lower muscularity and that the superior muscularity is due to the leg having a higher muscle to bone mass ratio, which is associated with a higher yield of boneless cuts and a longer femur.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the most important factors affecting the quality of meat and carcasses.
the development of an objective method for assessing muscularity of lamb carcasses and the relationship between muscularity and meat yield.
the development of objective measures of lamb carcass muscularity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the superior muscularity of the E-class group is reflected in a higher yield of leg plus saddle cuts (4.3%), a higher yield of boneless leg cuts (6.5%), a higher muscle to bone mass ratio (13.6%), a higher 'eye'-muscles area (A) (8.2%) and depth (B) (8.4%), and a higher muscularity index (14.2%) in the femur and thigh region of carcasses.
, although there is a slight difference in yield, the major difference in carcasses of superior muscularity is in the shape of the leg, which is a consequence of the shape of the femur.
the selection of lamb carcasses for higher muscularity will result in carcasses that have slightly higher yield and greater muscle depth relative length of bone in the femur and tibia regions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the E class carcass is a good one for meat yield, but the consumer might be more concerned with the shape of the carcass or cut.
the E class is more muscular than the Non-E class and the E-class lambs are more muscular than non-E-class lambs, but the differences are small.
carcasses of lambs selected for high muscularity will have a greater yield of boneless leg and saddle cuts and greater leg muscularity, and will also have greater 'eye' muscle area.
The main takeaway from our work is that
carcasses with higher muscularity will not necessarily yield more meat than other carcasses.
there is a clear association between carcass shape and the amount of muscle in the leg, but that the association is weak.
the E class is a useful selection tool for producers who are seeking to increase carcass yield and muscle depth.
